Done for the model with a fitted kurtosis per site without hyperlaw.

# Explanatory variables {.unnumbered}

We chose the following summary statistics:

- the turnover rate $\omega$;

- the total over-productivity and over-mortality are estimated as the area under the curve of the short-term process:

- $\frac{\delta e^2 \tau}{4}$ for productivity;

- $\frac{\alpha}{\lambda}$ for mortality;

- the time taken to reach 95% of the total over-productivity and mortality (i.e. the duration of the change in fluxes):

- the numerical solution to the equation: $e^{-\frac{2}{\tau} t_{95}}(\frac{t_{95}^2}{2\tau}+\frac{t_{95}}{2}+\frac{\tau}{4})=\frac{\tau}{80}$ for productivity;

- $t_{95} = \frac{ln(20)}{\lambda}$ for mortality.

```{r}
plot_info <- read.csv("data/raw_data/bioforest-plot-information.csv") |>
  left_join(read.csv("data/raw_data/plot_correspondance.csv")) |>
  mutate(thinning = grepl("hinning|evitali", Treatment_original)) |>
  select(site, plot = new_plot, Year_of_harvest, Treatment, thinning) |>
  unique()

data <- read.csv("data/derived_data/aggregated_data_v10.csv") |>
  left_join(plot_info, by = join_by(Site == site, Plot == plot)) |>
  filter(grepl("^agb", variable) & !grepl("]$", variable)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = "variable", values_from = "value") |>
  mutate(prod = agb_growth + agb_recr, mort = agb_mort, stocks = agb) |>
  select(!contains("agb")) |>
  group_by(Site, plot_new = Plot) |>
  arrange(Year) |>
  mutate(tdiff = c(0, diff(Year))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c("stocks", "prod", "mort"), names_to = "variable") |>
  mutate(Year_of_harvest = ifelse(Site == "Mbaiki" & Treatment == "Logging",
    1985, Year_of_harvest
  )) |>
  mutate(Year_of_harvest = ifelse(Site == "Paracou" & Treatment == "Logging",
    1987, Year_of_harvest
  )) |>
  mutate(trec = Year - Year_of_harvest) |>
  ## tapajos: second logging in 2014-2015
  filter(!(Site == "Tapajos Km67" & (Year >= 2014 | grepl("later", Plot)))) |>
  # remove plots with post-logging treatments
  filter(!thinning)
```

## Effect of environmental variables

```{r}
environ <- readr::read_tsv("data/raw_data/environment.tsv")
params <- read.csv("data/derived_data/params_flux_all.csv")
```

```{r}
environ |>
  group_by(site) |>
  summarise(dsi = mean(dsi)) |>
  inner_join(filter(params, variable == "omega"), by = join_by(site == Site)) |>
  ggplot(aes(dsi, median, col = site)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = q5, ymax = q95)) +
  labs(x = "Dry season intensity", y = "AGB turnover rate") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
environ |>
  group_by(site) |>
  summarise(dsi = mean(dsi)) |>
  inner_join(filter(params, variable == "t90p"), by = join_by(site == Site)) |>
  ggplot(aes(dsi, median, col = site)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = q5, ymax = q95)) +
  labs(
    x = "Dry season intensity",
    y = "AGB overproductivity duration [ yr ]"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Effect of logging intensity

```{r}
sites <- read.csv("data/derived_data/sites_to_keep.csv") |>
  filter(ncensus >= 10)
read.csv("data/derived_data/aggregated_data_v10.csv") |>
  rename_with(tolower) |>
  filter(site %in% sites$Site & variable == "agb") |>
  left_join(plot_info) |>
  group_by(site) |>
  mutate(agb_control = mean(value[Treatment == "Control"])) |>
  group_by(site, plot, Treatment) |>
  summarise(
    agb_0 = ifelse(Year_of_harvest <= min(year),
      agb_control, value[year == min(year)]
    ),
    pre = ifelse(Year_of_harvest <= min(year), "no", "yes"),
    agb_min = min(value[year > Year_of_harvest & year <= Year_of_harvest + 5])
  ) |>
  mutate(intensity = (agb_0 - agb_min) / agb_0) |>
  inner_join(filter(params, variable == "stpp"),
             by = join_by(site == Site, plot == plot_new)) |>
  ggplot(aes(intensity * 100, median / agb_0 * 100, col = site, shape = pre)) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, lty = 2) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = q5 / agb_0 * 100, ymax = q95 / agb_0 * 100)) +
  labs(
    x = "Logging intensity [% initial AGB]",
    y = "AGB total overproductivity [% initial AGB]",
    shape = "Has pre-logging inventory?"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
